questions.question: The front brake is:

options.text: Safe no matter how you use it.
Only for use if the rear brake fails.

questions.explanation: The front brake is safe when used properly. It is more powerful than the rear brake and provides most of your stopping power.

questions.question: Before every ride, you should check all of the following except:
questions.explanation: Before every ride, check your motorcycle carefully. Look at the rims and spokes for damage or looseness. Check your tire condition and tread. Check all lights.

questions.question: A rectangular sign can be a:
questions.explanation: Signs that show road rules, like speed limits, are rectangular with white backgrounds and black letters or symbols. You must follow the rules on these signs.

questions.question: What can you do to be seen better at an intersection?

options.text: Swerve within your lane to get attention.

questions.explanation: To be seen better at an intersection, use your headlight and position your motorcycle where oncoming traffic can see you best. Leave space around your motorcycle so you can move quickly if needed.

questions.question: A simple way to make your motorcycle easier to see is to:

options.text: Add a large flag to its frame.
Ride on the shoulder whenever possible.

questions.explanation: Keep your headlight on at all times. Use bright, reflective clothing. Use your turn signals and brake light correctly.

questions.question: ____ can remove alcohol from your body.
questions.explanation: Only time removes alcohol from your body. Coffee, exercise, fresh air, and cold showers do not reduce alcohol effects. They may keep you awake, but they do not make you sober.

questions.question: Which of the following is not protective clothing for a motorcycle rider?
questions.explanation: Safe riding gear includes a helmet, eye protection, a jacket, long pants, sturdy boots, and gloves.

questions.question: When downshifting, you should:

options.text: Shift down one gear at a time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift down one gear at a time.
questions.explanation: When downshifting, shift to one lower gear at a time. Release the clutch slowly between each downshift.

questions.question: Which type of footwear is best for a motorcycle operator?
questions.explanation: Sturdy boots that support your ankles offer the best protection. Laced-up boots work best. If you wear shoes with long laces, tuck them in before riding.

questions.question: To get the most protection from a helmet, choose one that:

options.text: Has been in a crash before.

questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) standards. Your helmet should fit snugly all the way around your head.

questions.question: What should a motorcyclist do to stay safe when riding on a slippery surface?
questions.explanation: On a slippery surface, slow down to stay safe. Sudden moves can cause your motorcycle to slide. Do not ride on the shoulder to avoid slippery roads.

questions.question: For the best protection, jackets and pants should:

options.text: Cover your arms and legs completely.
Be loose and flap in the wind while riding.
Only partially cover your arms and legs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cover your arms and legs completely.
questions.explanation: Jackets and pants should cover your arms and legs completely. They should fit snugly but allow you to move freely. Leather or synthetic materials offer the best protection in an accident.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, you should wear a jacket:

options.text: Only on rides longer than half an hour.

questions.explanation: Always wear a long-sleeved jacket when riding, even in warm weather. It protects you from the sun and dehydration.

questions.question: Which hand controls the accelerator on a motorcycle?
questions.explanation: The accelerator is on the right handgrip and is controlled with your right hand.

questions.question: Why is it better to keep a group of riders small?

options.text: A small group stays together better in traffic than a large group.
A small group can ignore traffic laws to stay together.
Riders always have to catch up to the group.
It is hard to keep track of everyone.

questions.correctAnswerText: A small group stays together better in traffic than a large group.
questions.explanation: Small groups have advantages. They are easier for other vehicles to pass, less likely to get separated by traffic or stop lights, and create less pressure for slower riders to speed up.

questions.question: When riding on a bridge grating, you should:

options.text: Always ride on the far right side of the lane.
Always ride on the far left side of the lane.
Stay relaxed, keep a steady speed, and ride straight across.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay relaxed, keep a steady speed, and ride straight across.
questions.explanation: Bridge gratings may cause your motorcycle to weave. This is usually safe, so relax and cross at a steady speed. Zigzagging to avoid the weave is dangerous because it forces you out of your lane.

questions.question: When alcohol and drugs are used together, their effects:

options.text: Are stronger than when either is used alone.
Are less dangerous than when either is used alone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Are stronger than when either is used alone.
questions.explanation: Many drugs, including prescription and over-the-counter medicines, can reduce your riding ability. Combining drugs with alcohol makes them even more dangerous.

questions.question: How can a motorcycle operator slow down?
questions.explanation: Motorcyclists can slow down by downshifting. Be aware that downshifting does not activate the brake lights.

questions.question: Signals on a motorcycle are:

options.text: More important than signals on larger vehicles.
Only needed when another vehicle is next to the motorcycle.
Less important than signals on larger vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: More important than signals on larger vehicles.
questions.explanation: Because motorcyclists are more vulnerable than car and truck drivers, using signals is even more important for motorcyclists.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They warn drivers about upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: Shifting into a lower gear has an effect similar to:
questions.explanation: Shifting into a lower gear slows your motorcycle. This is called engine braking.

questions.question: What clothing should you wear when riding a motorcycle?

options.text: Cover your arms and legs completely.
Cover your arms completely, but leave your legs exposed.
Cover your legs completely, but leave your arms exposed.
Wear whatever is most comfortable, regardless of safety.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cover your arms and legs completely.
questions.explanation: Wear a jacket and pants that cover your arms and legs completely. This protects you in case of an accident.

questions.question: When passing parked cars, a motorcycle rider should be ready for:

options.text: A car to suddenly pull out of a parking space into traffic.
Other drivers to see you and stay out of your way.

questions.correctAnswerText: A car to suddenly pull out of a parking space into traffic.
questions.explanation: A parked car may suddenly pull into traffic without warning. Ride on the left side of your lane when passing parked cars on your right. This gives you more space to avoid them.

questions.question: What should you do if someone is tailgating you?

options.text: Change lanes and let them pass.
Use your horn and make obscene gestures.
Speed up to create distance between you and them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: Change lanes and let the tailgater pass. Speeding up only makes them follow you at higher speeds, which is more dangerous.

questions.question: When should you do a pre-ride inspection?
questions.explanation: Check your motorcycle before every ride. This only takes a few minutes and helps prevent problems before you ride.
